sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Physical Wholesale Brokerage of Marine Fuel Oil and Distillates

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: Independent State of Samoa (Malo Sa'oloto Tuto'atasi o Samoa); constitutional monarchy and member of the Commonwealth of Nations
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa International Companies offshore financial centre (unitary national jurisdiction with no sub-state tax or regulatory distinctions)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law base, modified by the Constitution and Samoan customary law; offshore corporate statutes follow BVI-model common law precedent)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) with Australia (signed 2009; in force 2010)
Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) with New Zealand (signed 2009; in force 2010)
TIEA commitments with Nordic jurisdictions (Denmark, Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden) concluded 2011-2012
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus), signed 14 June 2017, in force 13 December 2020 (trade and investment facilitation framework)
ACP-EU Partnership Agreement (Cotonou successor), signed in Apia, Samoa on 15 November 2023 (Samoa Agreement)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Acts 2008, 2009, 2011 and 2014, including mandatory beneficial-ownership record-keeping; International Companies Regulations 2008; International Companies Fees Regulations; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 (Samoa) and Money Laundering Prevention Regulations 2019; Financial Intelligence Unit operating under the Central Bank of Samoa.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level_note: Samoa maintains no public UBO register. The licensed international company agent is legally obliged to identify, verify and retain current beneficial-ownership information for inspection by the Registrar of International Companies and the Financial Intelligence Unit. Nominee shareholders and directors are permitted, but the natural-person UBOs must be recorded and disclosed on lawful demand.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of any corporate shareholder (parent entity), certified copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the parent entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Samoa is a Contracting Party to the Hague Apostille Convention, in force 3 September 2016); Consular Legalization only if issued outside a Convention state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Register of Directors and Officers for any existing corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed international company agent or corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (for Samoa-issued documents) or foreign competent apostille authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport page of each UBO, director, shareholder and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization depending on the notary's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, issued within 3 months) for each UBO and director
Bank reference letter (banker's due-diligence confirmation of account conduct and source of funds capacity) for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Existing relationship bank of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization; bank-to-bank SWIFT confirmation may substitute in correspondent practice

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source of Wealth and Source of Funds declaration, including supporting evidence of lawful origin of liquid capital for commodity-trading operations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: UBO or beneficial owner, executed before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended - ss. 4-8 (Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles), ss. 21-26 (Registered Office), ss. 45-60 (Directors and Officers), ss. 200-210 (Tax Exemption); International Companies (Fees) Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of an International Company (Form prescribed under s. 6 of the International Companies Act 1987) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow or capital deposit requirement. Shares may be par or no-par value and denominated in any major currency. A security bond or bank guarantee may be required only at the petroleum licence stage.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the initial subscriber shares of the Company, as set forth in the Memorandum of Association, be and are hereby ratified, allotted, and accepted at par, with share certificates issued accordingly.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office be fixed at the licensed registered agent's office in Apia, Samoa, who is authorized to accept legal process for the Company.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed Director and [Name] appointed Corporate Secretary, each serving until removed by the Board.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Directors are authorized to open bank accounts, execute petroleum wholesale brokerage contracts, and take all lawful actions to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA - Registrar of International Companies, Apia, Samoa (submission via licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a completed Name Reservation Request listing up to three acceptable names ending in 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Ltd.', 'Corp.', or 'Inc.'. The registered agent verifies the Register for identical or confusingly similar names. Upon clearance, the name is reserved for 60 days.
required_dossiers: Licensed registered agent letter of engagement
Certified passport copy of the subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as undesirable or identical, submit alternate names within 5 business days; an adverse determination may be appealed to the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles in English with an objects clause authorising wholesale brokerage of crude oil, marine fuel oil, and refined petroleum distillates. Specify authorised share capital and subscriber allotments. The subscriber executes the documents before the registered agent, with signatures notarised.
required_dossiers: Drafted Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Returned documents may be corrected and re-executed within 10 working days without re-filing penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Registration, constitution documents, name clearance certificate, and the US$500 government filing fee via the licensed registered agent's online portal or countersigned hard copy. The Registrar examines statutory compliance and issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Minor deficiencies are curable by resubmission within 14 days; documents approved with conditions must be rectified within 30 days or the application lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and First Board Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA - Registrar of International Companies; Company Board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive the Certificate of Incorporation and the Company registration number. The subscriber passes the First Board Resolution appointing Directors, the Corporate Secretary, and the registered office. File the Notice of Directors and Secretary with SIFA within 21 days and issue share certificates.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the First Board Resolution
Notice of Directors and Secretary form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A defective Notice of Directors may be refiled in corrected form within the statutory notice period; late refiling attracts a nominal administrative fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Tax Exemption Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial banks in Samoa; SIFA Revenue Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate bank account using the Certificate of Incorporation, board resolution, and KYC documents. Obtain from SIFA a Certificate of Tax Exemption confirming freedom from income, withholding, and stamp duties under the International Companies Act for offshore operations.
required_dossiers: Corporate account opening application and KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The SIFA Tax Exemption Certificate may be expedited within 3 working days upon written consent of the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Petroleum Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Petroleum Wholesale Trade Licence application covering marine fuel oil and refined distillate brokerage. Submit corporate records, beneficial ownership declarations, an AML/CFT compliance manual, and a performance bond or bank guarantee if prescribed. The licence imposes enhanced KYC/AML obligations for transactions settled by standby letter of credit or SWIFT wire.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and register of directors
Performance bond or bank guarantee (if prescribed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Application queries must be answered within 15 days; the licence may be granted with conditions; refusal is appealable to the Minister responsible for petroleum.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Petroleum Division, in coordination with the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Petroleum Products Dealer / Wholesaler Licence (Petroleum Act 1984; Petroleum Products Marketing and Pricing Regulations 2004)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment, Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Preliminary Assessment / Registration for remote offshore trading with no physical fuel storage within Samoa. Category A - Full EIA Report required if bunkering operations, tank farms, or port-side storage vessels are located in Samoan waters.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet Water Resources Management Act 2008 thresholds: oil and grease <= 10 mg/L, COD <= 100 mg/L. Fugitive VOC releases must be negligible; vessels and bunkering operations must satisfy MARPOL Annex VI sulphur and NOx limits. Oily residues and contaminated fuel sludge must be manifested and disposed under the Waste Management Act 2011.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: FESA Fire Safety Certificate for any brokerage or storage premises, including fire detection, extinguishers, and a fuel-handling response plan. Structural load inspection certificate issued by the Land Transport Authority engineering inspectorate for tanks, containers, and equipment. Ministry of Health / OSHA Samoa workplace registration and a Hazardous Materials (HazMat) handling authorisation for marine fuel transfers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue, Samoa (MfR) — Taxpayer Administration System (TAS) portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: International Companies (ICs) under the International Companies Act 1987 are exempt from Samoan direct taxation and are NOT required to obtain a domestic TIN for offshore trading. The foreign parent/brokerage registers the IC with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL). A VAGST TIN is required only if the IC makes domestic taxable supplies in Samoa; application is filed via Form VAGST-1 on the TAS portal attaching the IC's certificate of incorporation, memorandum & articles, board resolution appointing a local process agent, and a registered Samoan address.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (IC: exempt from income tax, capital gains, dividend/distribution taxes, stamp duty, estate duty, gift duty, and foreign-exchange control; 20-year statutory exemption from commencement of business, renewable in practice)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or US-style entity classification election exists in Samoa. VAGST registration is compulsory once taxable turnover reaches WST 100,000 and is elective below that threshold; no hybrid mismatch elections apply (no hybrid rules enacted); ICs may elect in their constitutional documents to operate as exempt or limited companies under the IC Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) — strictly territorial; supplies of offshore goods and international freight to non-residents are outside scope
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 annual value of taxable supplies (VAGST Act 1994, s.7); registration effective within 21 days of the obligation arising
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API e-invoicing, or digital stamping regime in force. Registered suppliers must issue a valid VAGST invoice (supplier TIN, recipient name/TIN, date, description, VAGST amount) within 5 working days of supply; tax returns and refund claims are filed electronically via the TAS portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAGST applies to: (1) goods physically exported out of Samoa within 28 days of supply; (2) services supplied to a non-resident where the benefit is wholly offshore; (3) marine fuel and bunker supplies to ships engaged in international voyages / foreign-going vessels; (4) international air/sea transport. The IC's offshore brokerage of crude oil and refined products is structured either outside the Samoan VAGST net (non-resident counterparties, title passing offshore) or zero-rated if a Samoan supplier is contractually used.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs export declaration (CusDEC) with electronic customs clearance receipt
Original negotiable Bill of Lading / Sea Waybill evidencing offshore discharge port
Final commercial invoice and packing list
Signed sales contract (FOB/CIF/CFR terms) identifying buyer and physical delivery point
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing foreign currency settlement
Bunker delivery receipt (BDN) and independent quantity surveyor report for marine fuel parcels
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: MfR audits all zero-rated refund claims and may offset refunds against any outstanding tax liability. Shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 2012 scale at 25% (failure to take reasonable care), 50% (recklessness) and 75% (intentional disregard); fraudulent export claims trigger full retrospective clawback of refunds plus monthly late-payment interest (2% per month or part-month) and criminal prosecution of directors/officers, with deregistration and revocation of the IC's tax exemption as collateral sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), constituted under the Central Bank Act 2016, exercising delegated exchange-control powers through the Exchange Control Act 1975 and the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoa Tala (WST) is a non-internationally traded, managed-float currency. Current-account convertibility for bona fide trade and service payments is available through CBS-authorised dealers subject to transactional documentation; capital-account conversions and WST-denominated cross-border transfers require prior CBS exchange-control approval. Profit remittance for an International Company (IC) is substantially unhindered where the entity maintains fully foreign-currency (USD) accounts and funds are repatriated without conversion into WST. Dividends, return of capital, and liquidation proceeds may be freely wired to non-resident shareholders under the IC tax-exempt regime, supported by audited financial statements, a board resolution, and confirmation of good standing; no Samoan withholding tax applies to IC distributions. The residual hurdle arises only where funds are converted into or cleared through the domestic WST system, at which point an authorised dealer will require underlying transaction evidence and CBS forms for capital-account remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters are subject to CBS surrender requirements obligating repatriation of foreign-currency receipts through an authorised dealer within the statutory timeline (practically 30 to 90 days from shipment date) and conversion into WST absent an express retention quota or exemption granted by the CBS. The mandatory conversion ratio is applied at 100% of qualifying export receipts unless a waiver is secured. However, a Samoa International Company in the crude-oil and refined-products wholesale scope is treated as an offshore-exempt foreign-currency structure: export invoices booked offshore, denominated in USD, and settled into the IC's authorised-dealer foreign-currency account are outside the mandatory surrender regime, and no WST conversion is imposed. The exemption operates only while funds remain in the foreign-currency clearing circuit and the registered agent maintains the IC's exempt-status certificate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Capital Escrow Account / USD Operational Account (with dedicated trade-liquidity ledger)
USD Operational Settlement Account / Documentary Import-Export LC and SBLC Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility as a primary treasury rail. Samoa has no locally regulated Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing regime, and offshore digital EMIs (e.g., UK/FCA, EU/EMD passport holders) are not recognised as CBS-authorised dealers and cannot issue locally actionable Standby Letters of Credit or access the Samoan clearing infrastructure. Their practical utility is confined to ancillary FX conversion or pre-paid disbursement, which is lawfully insufficient for high-risk marine-fuel wholesale settlement. Use of an unlicensed EMI for core trade proceeds would breach Samoa's AML/CFT obligations attaching to IC registered agents and would materially damage the high-risk banking profile with any downstream correspondent bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a high-risk energy-commodity wholesale entity, CBS-licensed banks mandate a physical KYC interview at an Apia branch for the ultimate beneficial owner and at least two directors; fully remote account opening is not available in market practice. Video verification may abbreviate the documentary stage but does not replace the in-person interview. Where physical attendance is genuinely impracticable, a secondary route is accepted only on a discretionary basis comprising: Apostilled notarised identification packs, an introducer bank-to-bank reference from a recognised private-bank/correspondent, corroborated video-live interview, and registered-agent attestation; final refusal risk remains high without direct UBO presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse-media and sanctions exposure linked to petroleum trading with flagged jurisdictions, sanctioned vessels, or undisclosed chartering counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete corporate-tree chart with Samoan International Companies Act registration certificate; UN/OECD/OFAC sanctions-screening report covering counterparties, vessels, and banks; IMO/flag-state registry verification; independent legal opinion on cargo origin and derivative ownership; voyage-level bill-of-lading and marine-fuel assay documentation; CBS-compliant AML policy manual.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity through discretionary trusts, nominee arrangements, or layered offshore structures preventing UBO identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled trust deed or corporate-governance extract; statutory declaration of settlors and discretionary beneficiaries; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements for all material stakeholders; audited IC financial statements for three operating periods; bank references from tier-1 correspondent banks; registered-agent certificate attesting to the CBS/Financial Intelligence Unit customer-due-diligence file.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate SBLC/MT103 trade volumes relative to the IC's stated capital base, triggering structuring and round-tripping red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Back-to-back documentary trade contracts physically linking each SBLC utilisation to a marine-fuel cargo or refined-product parcel; third-party cargo survey and pricing benchmark reports; audited treasury ledger and receivables/payables age analysis; executed AML/CFT compliance program; legal opinion characterising the transactions as genuine physical wholesale rather than pure financial arbitrage.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: USD-denominated SWIFT MT103 wire transfers routed through global correspondents (New York Fedwire clearing) to a CBS-authorised Samoan dealer for credit to the IC's USD Capital Escrow Account. The wire must carry a truthful purpose code (economic category) reflecting equity injection, shareholder loan, or working-capital funding, accompanied by: board resolution approving the capital event, updated share register, UBO declaration, source-of-funds dossier, certificate of incorporation and IC tax-exempt status certificate. Bank reference and proof of business licence for ISIC 4661 must be pre-submitted. Where the individual transfer exceeds the dealer's internal CBS reporting threshold, CBS exchange-control formality/clearance should be sought in advance. Funds are held in escrow classification until trade registration and regulatory licence validation are completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational cash outflows (freight, brokerage commission, demurrage, storage, survey costs) are executed via SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary and purpose data referencing the underlying marine-fuel contract. Large-value physical settlements for crude oil and refined products are cleared through Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) under UCP600 and Standby Letters of Credit (MT760) under URDG758, with confirming-bank support where counterparty risk requires it. Same-day settlement for terminal deliveries may use MT199/MT202 cover instructions. All outward instructions must attach contract schedules, commercial invoices, bills of lading or delivery tickets, and quality certificates to satisfy the authorised dealer's trade-documentation audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST vanilla over-the-counter FX forward contracts executed through CBS-authorised dealers for residual local-cost exposures
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST for restricted-currency balance-sheet hedging where local liquidity is insufficient
Cross-currency swaps (USD versus EUR/JPY/AUD/SGD) for hedging procurement and resale cash-flow mismatches within the commodity supply chain
Commodity-linked total-return swap or equity-price hedge where economically aligned to physical distillate inventory and approved by the IC board

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual License Fee Renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On incorporation anniversary date; payable within 90-day grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late surcharge of 10% per month; persistent non-payment triggers Registrar-administered administrative strike-off after 6 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of WST 10 per day up to WST 500; unpaid penalties and prolonged default lead to administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) via Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to WST 100,000 plus imprisonment of officers for false declarations under the AML/CFT Act 2007

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Petroleum Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Suspension of petroleum trading license; daily penalty of WST 2,000 for continued unlicensed wholesale brokerage activity

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered if (i) shareholders holding at least 10% of issued voting shares demand one; (ii) the company is licensed under Samoa's AML-regulated financial services regime; or (iii) gross annual turnover exceeds WST 2,000,000 (approximately USD 700,000). Other International Companies remain audit-exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as permitted under the International Companies Act 1987; no separate Samoa Local GAAP applies to International Companies; books may be kept in any major currency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every International Company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register at its registered office. Share transfers require the register to be updated within 14 days of transfer, and an annual UBO confirmation must be filed together with the Annual Return. Failure to update constitutes a strict liability offence under the AML/CFT Act 2007.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 10,000 if audit is triggered; otherwise nil

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate for International Companies (IC) registered under the International Companies Act 1987 (ICA 1987). Section 207 grants a comprehensive exemption from income tax, capital gains tax, withholding taxes, stamp duty and all other Samoan taxes, charges, rates or levies. No VAT/GST registration obligation arises for offshore brokerage services supplied to non-residents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form CIT-1 (Company Income Tax Return) filed via the Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) e-Services electronic portal. An exempt IC does not file CIT-1; instead it files the International Companies Annual Return with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) acting for the Registrar of International Companies under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), accompanied by payment of the annual government fee.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CIT-1 must be filed within 6 months after the end of the accounting period (e.g., 30 June of the following calendar year for a 31 December year-end). The IC Annual Return and annual government fee fall due on the anniversary of incorporation, or as invoiced by SIFA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross commission and trading margin from wholesale brokerage of marine fuel oil, crude oil and refined distillates (ISIC 4661).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: enter 0. Offshore-source commission income of an IC is excluded from assessable income under ICA 1987 s.207 and the Income Tax Act 2012.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income derived from Samoan-source services, sales or performance within Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 0 unless the IC conducted domestic Samoan business in breach of the offshore-only condition. Any such income becomes assessable at 27% with penalty exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: brokerage commission expenses, freight, demurrage, charter hire, insurance, bank charges, professional fees and other directly allocable trading costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: no entry required; enter 0. A non-resident with a permanent establishment in Samoa may deduct expenses incurred in producing Samoan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (Box 1A + Box 1B minus Box 2).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: statutory result is 0. Non-resident without a PE: no Samoan-source income, no filing obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable at the 27% headline rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exempt IC: WST 0. Non-resident with attributable Samoan-source income pays 27% net of credits for withholding tax previously deducted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty tax of 10% of the assessed tax (minimum WST 100) plus a late payment penalty of 25% where tax remains unpaid 30 days after assessment, plus monthly interest at 2% per month on outstanding amounts. Wilful non-filing is a criminal offence punishable by fines up to 100 penalty units (each WST 100) and imprisonment up to 12 months. Failure to file the IC Annual Return results in SIFA late fees, automatic administrative strike-off, and prohibition on continuation or re-registration.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory rate under the Income Tax Act 2012 for dividends paid by a resident company to a non-resident; however, dividends distributed by an International Company are withheld at 0% by virtue of the ICA 1987 s.207 tax exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a double taxation agreement (DTA), the payee must submit to the Samoa Revenue Authority: (i) an application for treaty entitlement, (ii) a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the treaty-partner tax authority, (iii) a declaration of beneficial ownership, and (iv) supporting payment documentation (dividend resolution, interest contract or royalty licence). Upon approval, SRA issues a direction to the remitting bank to apply the reduced treaty withholding rate. Samoa has comprehensive DTAs principally with Australia, New Zealand and Norway, and applies the OECD Model exchange-of-information standard for all other jurisdictions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% statutory rate; treaty-reduced to 5% under the Australia-Samoa and New Zealand-Samoa DTAs and 10% under comparable treaty provisions. Interest: 15% statutory rate; treaty-reduced to 10%. Interest and royalties paid by an IC to non-residents are exempt from all Samoan withholding tax under ICA 1987 s.207.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa has not enacted a statutory Local File or Master File threshold in WST. As a prudential audit and commercial-banking benchmark for the petroleum trading sector, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation aligned with OECD Chapter V is expected where annual related-party commodity turnover exceeds WST 1,000,000 (approximately USD 375,000). The SRA can invoke general anti-avoidance and arm's-length powers in the Income Tax Act 2012 to demand comparability studies, pricing models and board documentation during audit.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) for benchmarked fuel oil price differentials and brokerage commissions
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2020 apply to ICs carrying on relevant activities, including a distribution and service centre, trading, holding-company and headquarter functions. A marine fuel brokerage IC must demonstrate in Samoa: (i) full-time qualified employees proportionate to the trading activity, (ii) physical premises and registered office, (iii) adequate operating expenditure, and (iv) core income-generating activities performed in Samoa, namely negotiation, contracting, fuel procurement, risk management and operational control of the SBLC/SWIFT payment cycle. An annual economic substance declaration must be filed with SIFA. Pure equity holding companies enjoy reduced substance requirements only.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Abuse of IC Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC as a de facto domestic trading or brokering business within Samoa, generating Samoan-source commissions while purporting to rely on the ICA 1987 s.207 exemption; failing to register and file CIT-1; issuing false annual returns to SRA or SIFA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SRA reassessment at 27% on the entire undeclared income, plus a 25% penalty tax on the deficiency, monthly interest at 2%, and deregistration of the company by the Registrar of International Companies. Criminal conviction carries fines up to 100 penalty units (WST 100 each) and imprisonment up to 12 months.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed false returns or directed domestic trading are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, penalty and interest; the corporate veil is pierced for tax debts where the company is used as a sham. Directors face travel prohibition orders, disqualification from acting as directors in Samoa for up to 10 years, and imprisonment for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Retaining registration in Samoa without a genuine registered office or licensed registered agent; maintaining no physical premises, staff or board records in Samoa; executing back-dated or sham physical fuel contracts solely to obtain commission paid into a Samoa foreign-currency bank account; declaring nil economic substance in the SIFA annual substance declaration while transacting millions of dollars in fuel brokerage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off and cancellation of IC registration under ICA 1987; refusal by SIFA to issue a Certificate of Good Standing; automatic exchange of information with OECD and treaty partners exposing the arrangement to foreign tax assessments. The Ministry of Industry and MCIL may impose regulatory fines of up to WST 50,000 for failure to maintain the registered agent requirement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the licensed agent may be held personally liable for restoration costs and outstanding annual fees; the corporate veil is pierced to attach personal liability for obligations incurred through the sham, and directors may be named in a Samoa international tax information exchange notice leading to travel bans and asset freezing in foreign jurisdictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Brokering crude oil or refined distillates for sanctioned entities or shell counterparties; accepting commission through opaque payment chains using Standby Letters of Credit and SWIFT wire transfers to conceal beneficial ownership; failing to conduct customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership disclosure, or transaction monitoring as required of a high-risk licensed entity; underwaluing or overvaluing fuel cargo to launder funds through commodity trades.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended), the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) may impose fines up to WST 1,000,000 per offence, suspend or revoke the statutory commodities trading licence, and refer the matter to the Samoa Law Society for professional sanction of the compliance officer, with parallel forfeiture proceedings over all related commission and held property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face personal fines up to WST 500,000, confiscation of trading proceeds, and imprisonment up to 14 years; conviction results in automatic disqualification from holding directorships in Samoan international companies for a decade, and travel bans may be imposed while an FIU money-laundering or terrorist-financing investigation is pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a nil or false economic substance declaration with SIFA for the FY while the IC derives substantial commission income from marine fuel brokerage; performing board deliberations, contract negotiation, fuel procurement and risk-management functions exclusively outside Samoa, in a jurisdiction with differing tax treatment, to secure tax exemption in Samoa and low taxation elsewhere.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2020, SIFA may impose a financial penalty of up to WST 250,000, require supplementary disclosure, strike the company off the register, and exchange the full tax-file with the foreign revenue authority of the beneficial owners, triggering imposition of foreign CFC or anti-avoidance levies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director who signed the false economic substance declaration is personally liable for the regulatory penalty and may be prosecuted criminally with imprisonment up to 3 years; directors become personally exposed to foreign tax-recovery claims under tax collection-assistance treaties, and the IC is reclassified as a fully taxable resident in the blacklisted or offshore-audit jurisdiction, subject to double taxation and 100% penalty loading.
